questions.question: In the mid - eighth century, Dantidurga, a Rashtrakuta chief, overthrew his Chalukya overlord and performed a ritual literally called a ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Golden Womb.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Golden Womb:-**

 
 
• It​ is a ritual performed by ancient Indian rulers to ensure the** birth of a son** who would be the rightful heir to the throne.
 
• This ritual involved the king lying down on a **bed of gold** and his queen sitting on his lap.
 
• The queen would then be blessed by the priests to** conceive a male child.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subsidiary alliance:-**

 
 
• It was a treaty between an Indian state and the British East India Company, under which the Indian state would provide the Company with troops and money in exchange for protection from external attack.
 
• The Indian state would also be required to accept a British Resident at its court, who would advise the ruler on all matters of foreign policy.

questions.question: The percentage of eligible voters who cast their votes in an election is termed as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Turnout.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Turnout:-**

 
 
• It​ is the percentage of **eligible voters **who cast their **votes in an election.**
 
• Turnout is an important measure of **voter engagement **and participation in the **democratic process.**
 
• It indicates the level of** interest, motivation, and civic responsibility** among the electorate.
 
• Turnout can vary widely depending on various factors such as the **type of election, the candidates or issues at stake, the timing and location** of the election, the level of political awareness and mobilization, and the accessibility and convenience of the voting process.
 
• Turnout can also have significant implications for the outcome of an election.
 
• A high turnout generally favors the candidate or party with broader appeal and support, while a low turnout can benefit the **candidate or party** with more **motivated and committed supporters.**
 
• Turnout can be influenced by various factors such as** voter registration laws, voter education and outreach programs, campaign strategies** and messaging, media coverage and social media trends, and the overall political climate and mood of the electorate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quorum:-**

 
 
• It refers to the **minimum number of member**s required for a** valid decision-making process** in a group or organization.
 
 
 
• **Veto:-**
 
 
• It​ refers to the power of a person or body to** reject or block a decision** or proposal.
 
 
 
• **Constituency:-**
 
 
• It​** **refers to the geographic area or** group of voters** represented by an elected official.

questions.question: Who was the last tirthankara of the Jainas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vardhamana Mahavira.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vardhamana Mahavira:-**

 
 
• Also known as Mahavira, was an important figure in Jainism.
 
• **He was the 24th Tirthankara ("ford-maker" or spiritual teacher) of Jainism. **
 
• Mahavira was born in 599 BC and died in 527 BC, though different sources may vary slightly in the exact dates.
 
• Mahavira taught a philosophy of asceticism and self-restraint focused on non-violence (ahimsa), truth (satya), non-stealing (asteya), chastity (brahmacharya), and non-possession (aparigraha). These five principles collectively form the main pillars of Jain ethical code.
 
 
 
• **Jainism:-**
 
 
• It is an ancient Indian religion that emphasizes **non-violence, self-control, and spiritual liberation** through the practice of austerities and meditation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandraprabha:-**

 
 
• He was the eighth Tirthankara (spiritual teacher). He is an important figure worshipped and respected by Jains. 
 
 
 
• **Rishabhanatha:-**
 
 
• He is also known as Rishabhadeva or Adinatha.
 
• He is considered the first Tirthankara (spiritual teacher) in Jain tradition.
 
• Rishabhanatha is a savior and spiritual guide who is believed to have formed the bridge between the mortal world and the divine.
 
 
 
• **Padmaprabha:-**
 
 
• He is the sixth Tirthankara (spiritual teacher) of Jainism.
 
• Born into a royal family, Padmaprabha took the path of asceticism after growing disenchanted with material pursuits and pleasures.

questions.question: As of 11 August 2022, who is the Chairman of Rajya Sabha?

• The members of the Rajya Sabha are elected or nominated for a term of six years.
 
• The nominated members of the Rajya Sabha are usually experts in various fields and have the same powers and privileges as the elected members.
 
• The nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha is done to ensure that the house has a diverse representation of people from different backgrounds and fields.
 
• The President of India can nominate members to the Rajya Sabha under Article 80(1)(a) of the Constitution of India.

• The Chairman of Rajya Sabha is the Vice President of India, who is currently** Venkaiah Naidu. **

questions.question: Indian constitution borrowed cabinet form of governance from ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United Kingdom.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cabinet form of governance:-**

 
 
• It​ is a system of government where the executive branch is led by a** cabinet of ministers **who are chosen from the legislature.
 
• The Indian constitution borrowed this form of governance from the** United Kingdom**, which is known for its **parliamentary system of government.**
 
• The cabinet system in India is headed by the **Prime Minister,** who is the leader of the majority party in the** Lok Sabha, **the lower house of the Indian parliament.
 
• The cabinet ministers are appointed by the **President on the advice of the Prime Minister** and they are collectively responsible to the parliament.
 
• The cabinet system in India has undergone changes over the years, but it remains one of the** key features **of the Indian political system.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **France:-**

 
 
• It​ has a **semi-presidential system** of government.
 
• The president is the head of state and the Prime Minister is the head of government.
 
 
 
• **South Africa:-**
 
 
• It** **has a** parliamentary system of government.**
 
• The President is the head of state and the Prime Minister is the head of government.
 
 
 
• **Australia:-**
 
 
• It​** **also has a **parliamentary system of government.**
 
• The Prime Minister is the head of government.
 
• However, the cabinet system in Australia is different from that of India, as the ministers are appointed by the **Governor-General** on the advice of the Prime Minister.

questions.question: Meena talks about an example of sedimentary rock. Which one of the following can it be?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sandstone.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sedimentary rocks:-**

 
 
• These​ are formed by the accumulation of **sediments over time,** which get compacted and cemented together.
 
• **Sandstone **is a common example of sedimentary rock. 
 
• **Sandstone **is composed of **sand-sized grains **of mineral, rock, or organic material that have been transported by wind, water, or ice and deposited in layers.
 
• Over time, the grains get compacted and cemented together to form a** solid rock.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Granite** is a common type of **intrusive igneous rock** that is typically composed of **feldspar, quartz, and mica.**

 
 
• It is often used as a **building stone **and for** decorative purposes.**
 
 
 
• **Marble **is a metamorphic rock that is prized for its** beauty and durability.**
 
 
• It is often used in **sculpture and building construction. ** 
 
 
 
• **Basalt** is a **dark-colored volcanic rock **that is often used in construction and road-building due to its strength and durability.

questions.question: GDP is an indicator of a country’s economy. What does ‘D’ in GDP stand for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Domestic.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• GDP stands for** Gross Domestic Product,** which is the total value of goods and services produced within a country's borders in a **specific time period.**
 
• The 'D' in GDP refers to the** domestic aspect** of the country's economy, meaning that only **goods and services **produced within the country's borders are included in the calculation.
 
• The **rate of GDP growth** is a crucial gauge of a **nation's economic health.**
 
• A **nation's level of consumption, investment, government spending on goods and services,** and the **profit margin between exports and imports** can all be included in an equation to represent GDP.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Development **is a term used to describe the** growth and progress** of a country's economy over time.
 
• **Dividend** refers to the payment made to **shareholders of a company. **
 
• **Deficit** refers to a situation where a** country's expenses exceed** its revenue.

questions.question: In cricket, hitting the ball to the boundary along the ground is ______ runs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hitting the ball to the boundary** along the ground in cricket is worth **4 runs.**
 
• This is called a **"boundary" **and is achieved when the ball crosses the** outer edge of the playing field **without being caught or touching the ground outside the boundary.
 
• If the ball is hit in the air and crosses the boundary, it is worth **6 runs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Cricket is a sport played with a **bat and ball**, with two teams of **11 players** each.
 
• The objective of the game is to** score more runs** than the opposing team.
 
• Runs are scored by **hitting the ball **and running between **two sets of wickets, **or by hitting the ball to the boundary.

questions.question: The census of India is conducted at an interval of______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 years.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The census of India is conducted at an** interval of 10 years.**
 
• The first census in India was conducted in **1872.**
 
• As of **2021**, India's decennial census has been carried out **15 times. **
 
• The **first comprehensive census** was done in **1881,** but it had been conducted **every ten years** since **Viceroy Lord Mayo** took office in **1872.**
 
• Since **1949,** it has been managed by the **Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India**, through the **Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India. **
 
• The **1948 Census of India Act**, which predates the Indian Constitution, has been used to conduct all censuses since **1951.**
 
• The Union Government is not required by the **1948 Census of India Act** to carry out the Census on a specific day or to make the results available within a specified timeframe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The census provides information on the** size, distribution, and socio-economic** characteristics of the population.
 
• The latest census in India was conducted in** 2011,** and the next one is scheduled for **2021.**

questions.question: The rock - cave temple of ______ is the largest monolithic structure in the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ellora.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **rock-cave temple** referred to in the question is the **Kailasa Temple** located in the **Ellora Caves complex **in **Maharashtra, India.**
 
• The Kailasa Temple was carved out of a **single rock **in the** 8th century AD **and is considered a marvel of **Indian rock-cut architecture.**
 
• The temple complex covers an area of** 2 acres** and is **164 feet wide, **109 feet long, and 98 feet high.
 
• The temple features intricate carvings and sculptures depicting **Hindu mythology** and is dedicated to Lord Shiva.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Udayagiri caverns** are a group of **20 rock-cut caverns** close to **Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh.**

 
 
• They have been largely associated with the** Hindu gods Vishnu and Shiva** from the early **5th century CE. **
 
 
 
• **The 29 Buddhist cave monuments** known as the **Ajanta Caves** are located in the Maharashtra state's** Aurangabad District.**
 
 
• **​They** date from the second century **BCE to roughly 480 CE.**
 
 
 
• The **Badami cave temples** are situated in the town of Badami in **Karnataka, **India's north-central region.
 
 
• **Hindu and Jain** cave temples can be found together in the **Badami cave templ**e complex.

questions.question: Lala Lajpat Rai was an active member of which organisation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arya Samaj.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai** was an active member of **Arya Samaj,** a Hindu reformist movement that aimed to promote the principles o**f Vedas **and to oppose the** caste system and idol worship.**
 
• He was also one of the founding members of the **Indian National Congress** and played a key role in the Indian independence movement.
 
• **Arya Samaj:**
 
 
• Arya Samaj is regarded as a **monotheistic Indian Hindu reform movement** that upholds **moral principles and ethical behavior **in accordance with the conviction that the Vedas are **infallible. **
 
• **Dayanand Saraswati,** an austere sannyasi, founded the samaj in the** 1870s.**
 
• The first Hindu group to introduce **proselytization** inside **Hinduism **was Arya Samaj.
 
• Since the 1800s, the group has also campaigned to **advance the civil rights struggle** in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmo Samaj** was another** Hindu reformist movement **founded by** Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828 **that aimed to promote monotheism and social reform.
 
• **Brahmo Sabha** was an earlier version of **Brahmo Samaj founded in 1828** that later split into different factions.
 
• **Prathana Sabha** was a religious society founded by **Keshub Chandra Sen,** a disciple of **Raja Ram Mohan Roy, in 1867** that aimed to promote social and religious reform.
